extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, litigators, judges, and policy-makers working with or implementing the Unified Patent Court Rules of Procedure
extracted.subtask_description: High-level summary of the Unified Patent Court (UPC) Rules of Procedure: key features of UPC proceedings, recurring drafting/implementation issues (hot topics), and specific procedural provisions (e.g., public access under Rule 262 and opt-out mechanics). Intended as guidance for practitioners and stakeholders preparing for UPC litigation or rule implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: One year for a judgment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a main feature/expectation of UPC proceedings: target or typical timescale from commencement to final judgment is one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mainly written proceedings, in electronic form
rubrics_metrics.description: Mainly written proceedings, in electronic form
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings are predominantly based on written submissions and are handled electronically, implying emphasis on high-quality, complete written pleadings and e-filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Registrar: an important person
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Registrar plays a significant administrative and case-management role within UPC practice; practitioners should engage with and follow Registrar-driven procedures and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preformatted proceedings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of standardized forms/templates and preformatted procedural steps is a feature of UPC process design — parties must conform to prescribed formats and templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-loading system
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The UPC employs a front-loading approach: parties are expected to present the bulk of factual material and legal argumentation early in the proceedings. Drafting should prioritize early, comprehensive submissions and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Judge-rapporteur: a key person
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The judge-rapporteur has a central role in decision-making (e.g., deciding public access requests under Rule 262 after consulting parties) and in case management; practitioners should target and anticipate interactions with the judge-rapporteur.

rubrics_metrics.name: One day hearing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral hearings are typically short — often limited to a single day — which emphasizes the importance of concise oral presentation and thorough written pleadings beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing of a witness in person exceptional
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing of a witness in person exceptional
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal testimony by witnesses is exceptional; expect written witness statements and limited in-person witness hearings only in special circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal widely open
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The UPC appellate regime allows broad scope for appeal (the slide text: 'Appeal widely open'); practitioners should be prepared for extensive appellate opportunities and corresponding strategic considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court’s fees
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court fees are a notable feature of UPC proceedings and a factor in case strategy (cost of bringing/defending actions, opt-outs etc.). The slides flag fees as an important consideration but do not provide fee schedules on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opt-out provisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slide lists key practical questions about opt-out: 'Why? any reason to pay fees for status quo?' 'How much? "administrative level" or more?' 'Who? all proprietors' 'What? SPC goes with patent' 'For how long? life of the patent' 'Where? sunrise period EPO, Registry'. Guidance implies opt-out mechanics cover scope (who may opt-out), cost, whether related rights like SPCs are included, duration (up to life of patent), and registration venues (EPO sunrise period and UPC Registry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietorship and registration for opt-out and for proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proprietorship and registration for opt out and for proceedings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues around establishing proprietorship and the correct register entries for (i) the opt-out, and (ii) for initiating proceedings; accuracy of ownership records is crucial for both opting out and commencing UPC cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of the Statement of claim / language of the proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Language of the Statement of claim; language of the proceedings when Contracting Member States designate EPO official languages
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language selection for the statement of claim and for proceedings is a hot topic: where Contracting Member States designate one or more EPO official languages for local/regional divisions, practitioners must observe the designated language(s) and related translation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bifurcation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bifurcation (separation of infringement and validity proceedings) is a contested procedural issue in the UPC Rules drafting and practice; practitioners should plan litigation strategies considering potential bifurcation rules and court practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on provisional measures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rules and practice concerning provisional measures (e.g., interim injunctions, provisional relief) are a drafting focus; practitioners need to understand standards and timelines for obtaining provisional relief in the UPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decisions (permanent injunctions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules governing final relief — such as permanent injunctions — were a hot topic during drafting; parties should expect UPC rules and jurisprudence on scope and remedies for permanent relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave for procedural appeals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether leave (permission) is required for procedural appeals is an important procedural question addressed in the Rules; parties should assess appealability and leave requirements for interlocutory or procedural matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representatives authorised to practice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Who is authorised to represent parties before the UPC (qualification/registration of representatives) is a drafting/implementation issue; ensure compliance with representative authorisation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to register / publication and access rules (Rule 262)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text from Rule 262 (25 July 2022) concerning public access to the register: '1. Without prejudice to Articles 58 and 60(1) of the Agreement and subject to Rules 190.1, 194.5, 196.1, 197.4, 199.1, 207.7, 209.4, 315.2 and 365.2, and following, where applicable, redaction of personal data within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and confidential information according to paragraph 2 (a) decisions and orders made by the Court shall be published, (b) written pleadings and evidence, lodged at the Court and recorded by the Registry shall be available to the public upon reasoned request to the Registry; the decision is taken by the judge-rapporteur after consulting the parties.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 262 establishes transparency with important caveats: publication of decisions and orders is expected, and written pleadings/evidence may be made public upon reasoned request. Access is subject to other rules and redaction obligations (GDPR personal data and confidential information), and the judge-rapporteur decides on access after consulting the parties. Practitioners must consider confidentiality, data protection and the possibility of redaction when filing materials.
